title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Circular on Issuing the Opinions on Certain Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation)

Fa (Ban) Fa [1988] No. 6

To all local people's courts at various levels, all military courts, all railway transport intermediate courts and basic courts, and all maritime courts:

The Opinions on Certain Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation) are hereby issued to you for trial implementation in civil trial work and economic trial work. During the trial implementation, attention should be paid to investigation, research, and summarization of experience. Any opinions or questions should be promptly reported to this Court.

April 2, 1988

Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Certain Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation)

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on January 26, 1988)

The General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of Civil Law) came into effect on January 1, 1987. The following opinions are hereby proposed regarding issues encountered during the implementation of the General Principles of Civil Law.

I. Citizens

(1) Issues Concerning Capacity for Civil Rights and Capacity for Civil Conduct

1. A citizen's capacity for civil rights shall commence at birth. The time of birth shall be determined based on the household registration certificate; in the absence of a household registration certificate, it shall be determined based on the birth certificate issued by a hospital. In the absence of a hospital certificate, it shall be determined by reference to other relevant evidence.

2. A citizen who has reached the age of 16 but is under the age of 18, and who is able to obtain income through his or her own labor and maintain the general living standard of the local populace, may be deemed a person with full capacity for civil conduct whose main source of livelihood is his or her own labor income.

3. Whether a civil activity conducted by a minor who has reached the age of 10 is appropriate to his or her age and intelligence may be determined by reference to the degree of correlation between the act and the minor's personal life, whether the minor's intelligence enables him or her to understand the act and foresee the corresponding consequences of the act, and the amount involved in the act.

4. Whether a civil activity conducted by a mental patient who cannot fully discern his or her own conduct is appropriate to his or her mental health condition may be determined by reference to the degree of correlation between the act and the patient's personal life, whether the patient's mental state enables him or her to understand the act and foresee the corresponding consequences of the act, and the amount involved in the act.

5. A mental patient (including a person with dementia) who lacks the ability to judge and protect himself or herself and is unaware of the consequences of his or her conduct may be deemed a person who cannot discern his or her own conduct; a person who lacks the ability to judge and protect himself or herself with respect to relatively complex matters or relatively significant acts and cannot foresee the consequences of his or her conduct may be deemed a person who cannot fully discern his or her own conduct.

6. Where a person with no capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct accepts rewards, gifts, or remuneration, no other person may claim that such acts are invalid on the ground that the actor has no capacity for civil conduct or has limited capacity for civil conduct.

7. Whether a party suffers from a mental illness shall be confirmed by the people's court on the basis of a judicial psychiatric evaluation or by reference to a hospital's diagnosis or evaluation. Where conditions for diagnosis or evaluation are not available, it may also be confirmed by reference to the party's mental state as generally recognized by the public, provided that no interested party raises any objection.

8. In litigation, if a party or an interested party alleges that a party suffers from a mental illness (including dementia), and the people's court deems it necessary to confirm such fact, the court shall, in accordance with the special procedures stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), first render a judgment on whether the party has capacity for civil conduct.

Where a mental patient (including a person with dementia) is confirmed to be a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, the case shall be heard by reference to the special procedures stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

9. The place where a citizen has continuously resided for one year or more after leaving his or her domicile shall be deemed the habitual residence. However, this does not apply to a person who resides in a hospital for medical treatment.

Where a citizen, after moving out of his or her registered domicile and before moving into another place, has no habitual residence, the original registered domicile shall still be deemed his or her domicile.

(2) Issues Concerning Guardianship

10. A guardian's guardianship duties include: protecting the ward's physical health, caring for the ward's life, managing and protecting the ward's property, representing the ward in civil activities, managing and educating the ward, and representing the ward in litigation when the ward's lawful rights and interests are infringed upon or when the ward is involved in a dispute with others.

11. The determination of a guardian's capacity for guardianship shall be based on factors such as the guardian's physical health condition, financial circumstances, and the degree of connection in life with the ward.

12. "Close relatives" as stipulated in the General Principles of Civil Law include: spouse, parents, children, siblings, paternal grandparents, maternal grandparents, paternal grandchildren, and maternal grandchildren.

13. Where a guardian is to be appointed for a minor who suffers from a mental illness, the provisions of Article 16 of the General Principles of Civil Law shall apply.

14. When a people's court appoints a guardian, it may regard the order of subparagraphs (1), (2), and (3) of Paragraph 2 of Article 16, or subparagraphs (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5) of Paragraph 1 of Article 17, as the order of appointment of guardians. Where a person who has the qualifications for guardianship in the preceding order lacks the capacity for guardianship or is manifestly unfavorable to the ward, the people's court may, in accordance with the principle of being favorable to the ward, select and determine a guardian from among those who have the qualifications for guardianship in the subsequent order. If the ward has the capacity to discern, the ward's opinion shall be solicited as the circumstances warrant.

There may be one guardian, or multiple guardians from the same order.

15. Where persons who have the qualifications for guardianship agree among themselves to determine a guardian, the guardian determined by agreement shall assume guardianship responsibilities towards the ward.

16. Where there is a dispute over who shall serve as guardian, the relevant organization shall make the appointment in accordance with Paragraph 3 of Article 16 or Paragraph 2 of Article 17 of the General Principles of Civil Law. If a lawsuit is filed with a people's court without such prior appointment, the people's court shall not accept the case.

17. Where the relevant organization appoints a guardian in accordance with the provisions of the General Principles of Civil Law and notifies the appointed person in writing or orally, the appointment shall be deemed established. If the appointed person disagrees, he or she shall file a lawsuit with the people's court within 30 days from the day following receipt of the notice. If the lawsuit is filed after that period, it shall be handled as a change of guardianship relationship.

18. Once a guardian is appointed, he or she may not change the appointment unilaterally. If a change is made without authorization, both the originally appointed guardian and the changed guardian shall bear guardianship responsibilities.

19. Where the appointed person files a lawsuit against the appointment, the people's court shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 14 of these Opinions, render a judgment maintaining or revoking the appointment of the guardian. If the judgment revokes the original appointment, a different guardian may be appointed at the same time. Such cases shall be heard by reference to the special procedures stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

Pending the judgment of the people's court, guardianship responsibilities shall generally be borne by persons who have the qualifications for guardianship in accordance with the order of appointment of guardians.

20. Where a guardian fails to perform guardianship duties or infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of the ward, and other persons or units having the qualifications for guardianship as stipulated in Article 16 or Article 17 of the General Principles of Civil Law file a lawsuit with the people's court requesting that the guardian bear civil liability, the case shall be heard in accordance with ordinary procedures; if the request is for a change of guardianship relationship, it shall be heard in accordance with special procedures; if both a request for assumption of civil liability and a request for change of guardianship relationship are made, they shall be heard separately.

21. After divorce, the parent who lives with the child does not have the right to cancel the other parent's guardianship over the child; however, if the parent who does not live with the child commits a crime against the child, abuses the child, or is manifestly unfavorable to the child, and the people's court deems that cancellation is permissible, the guardianship may be cancelled.

22. A guardian may entrust part or all of the guardianship duties to another person. Where civil liability needs to be borne due to a tortious act of the ward, the guardian shall bear the liability, unless otherwise agreed; if the entrusted person is indeed at fault, he or she shall bear joint and several liability.

23. After the death of one spouse, if the other spouse gives the child up for adoption by another person, and the adoption is not detrimental to the child's healthy growth and legal adoption procedures have been completed, the adoption relationship shall be deemed established; other persons having the qualifications for guardianship may not claim that the adoption relationship is invalid on the ground that the adoption was not consented to by them.

(3) Issues Concerning Declaration of Missing Persons and Declaration of Death

24. Interested parties who may apply for declaration of a missing person include: the spouse, parents, children, siblings, paternal grandparents, maternal grandparents, paternal grandchildren, maternal grandchildren of the person to be declared missing, as well as other persons who have civil rights and obligations with the applicant.

25. The order of interested parties who may apply for declaration of death is:

(1) Spouse;

(2) Parents and children;

(3) Siblings, paternal grandparents, maternal grandparents, paternal grandchildren, maternal grandchildren;

(4) Other persons who have civil rights and obligations relationships.

An application for revocation of a declaration of death is not subject to the above order.

26. "Whereabouts unknown" refers to a situation where a citizen, after leaving his or her last place of residence, has had no news. A person who is in Taiwan or abroad and cannot communicate normally shall not be declared dead on the ground of being whereabouts unknown.

27. Where a person's whereabouts are unknown during a period of war, the period for applying for declaration of death shall be governed by the provisions of Subparagraph (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 23 of the General Principles of Civil Law.

28. The starting time of the period of being whereabouts unknown as referred to in Paragraph 1 of Article 20 and Subparagraph (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 23 of the General Principles of Civil Law shall be calculated from the day following the date when news of the citizen ceases.

Cases concerning declaration of missing persons shall be under the jurisdiction of the basic people's court in the place of domicile of the person to be declared missing. If the domicile and the place of residence are inconsistent, jurisdiction shall be with the basic people's court in the place of last residence.

29. Declaration of a missing person is not a prerequisite for declaration of death. If a citizen's whereabouts are unknown and the conditions for applying for declaration of death are met, interested parties may directly apply for declaration of death without first applying for declaration of missing person. However, if interested parties only apply for declaration of missing person, the declaration of missing person shall be made; if among interested parties in the same order, some apply for declaration of death and others do not agree to declaration of death, then declaration of death shall be made.

30. When a people's court appoints a property custodian for a missing person, it shall do so in accordance with the principle of protecting the missing person's property. If there is no custodian as specified in Article 21 of the General Principles of Civil Law, or if such custodians are incapable of serving as custodian or are unsuitable to serve as custodian, the people's court may appoint a citizen or a relevant organization as the property custodian for the missing person.

If a person with no capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct is missing, his or her guardian shall be the property custodian.

31. "Other expenses" as referred to in Paragraph 2 of Article 21 of the General Principles of Civil Law include necessary expenses such as maintenance fees, support fees, child-rearing fees, and management fees required for the administration of the property.

32. If the property custodian of a missing person refuses to pay taxes, debts, or other expenses owed by the missing person, and a creditor files a lawsuit, the people's court shall list the custodian as the defendant.

If the property custodian of a missing person demands repayment of debts from the missing person's debtor, the custodian may file a lawsuit as the plaintiff.

33. If a debtor's whereabouts are unknown but the debtor has not been declared missing, and a creditor files a lawsuit demanding repayment of the debt, the people's court may, after service of summons by public notice, render a default judgment or handle the case by suspending the proceedings.

34. When a people's court hears a case concerning declaration of a missing person, it shall do so by reference to the special procedures stipulated in the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

When a people's court hears a case concerning declaration of a missing person, it shall ascertain the property of the person to be declared missing, appoint a temporary administrator or take measures for preservation of the action, and issue a public notice seeking the missing person. The period of public notice shall be six months. Upon expiration of the public notice period, the people's court shall, based on whether the fact that the person to be declared missing is missing has been confirmed, render a judgment declaring the person missing or a ruling terminating the proceedings. If the judgment declares the person missing, a property custodian for the missing person shall be appointed at the same time.

35. If the property custodian of a missing person applies for a change of custodian on the ground of inability to perform custodial duties, the people's court shall hear the case by reference to special procedures.

If the property custodian of a missing person fails to perform custodial duties or infringes upon the property rights and interests of the missing person, interested parties of the missing person may request the people's court to make the property custodian bear civil liability. If an application is also made to the people's court for a change of property custodian, the action for change shall be heard separately by reference to special procedures.

36. For a person declared dead, the date of the judgment of declaration shall be the date of death. The judgment shall be served on the applicant and also be publicly announced in the place of domicile of the person declared dead and in the place where the people's court is located.

If the time of the declaration of death and the time of natural death are inconsistent, the legal consequences arising from the declaration of death shall remain effective; however, if a civil juristic act performed before the natural death contradicts the legal consequences arising from the declaration of death, the civil juristic act actually performed shall prevail.

37. The marital relationship between a person declared dead and his or her spouse shall terminate from the date of the declaration of death. If the declaration of death is revoked by the people's court, and the spouse has not remarried, the marital relationship shall be automatically restored from the date of revocation of the declaration of death; if the spouse remarries and later divorces, or if the spouse's subsequent spouse dies, the marital relationship shall not be deemed automatically restored.

38. If, during the period when a person is declared dead, his or her child is lawfully adopted by another person, and after the declaration of death is revoked, the person declared dead claims that the adoption relationship is invalid solely on the ground that it was not consented to by him or her, such claim shall generally not be allowed, except where both the adopter and the adopted person consent.

39. If an interested party, by concealing the true situation, causes another person to be declared dead and thereby obtains that person's property, the interested party shall, in addition to returning the property and its fruits, also compensate for the losses caused.

40. If a person whose declaration of death has been revoked requests the return of property, and the original property has been lawfully acquired by a third party, the third party may not be required to return it. However, a citizen or organization that acquired the original property by inheritance shall return the original property or provide appropriate compensation.

(4) Issues Concerning Individual Industrial and Commercial Households, Rural Contractual Operation Households, and Individual Partnerships

41. For an individual industrial and commercial household with a trade name, in civil litigation, the household head (proprietor) registered in the business license shall be the litigation party, and it shall be noted in the litigation documents that the party is the household head of a certain trade name.

42. If an individual industrial and commercial household registered in the name of an individual citizen, or a rural contractual operation household contracted by an individual, invests with family common property, or if the main portion of the income is enjoyed by family members, the debts shall be satisfied with the family common property.

43. During the existence of a marital relationship, if one spouse engages in individual business or contractual operation, the income shall be the common property of the spouses, and debts shall also be satisfied with the common property of the spouses.

44. When debts of an individual industrial and commercial household or a rural contractual operation household are to be satisfied with the family common property, necessary daily necessities for family members and necessary production tools shall be reserved.

45. For an individual partnership with a trade name, in civil litigation, the trade name approved and registered according to law shall be the litigation party, and the person in charge of the partnership shall be the litigation representative. The litigation acts of the person in charge of the partnership shall have legal effect on all partners.

For an individual partnership without a trade name, the partners shall be co-litigants in civil litigation. If there are many partners, litigation representatives may be elected to participate in the litigation. The litigation acts of the litigation representatives shall have legal effect on all partners. The election of litigation representatives shall be handled in writing.

46. A citizen who, in accordance with an agreement, provides funds or tangible property and agrees to participate in the distribution of partnership profits, but does not participate in the partnership's business operations or labor, or who provides technical services but does not provide funds or tangible property, and agrees to participate in the distribution of profits, shall be deemed a partner.

47. All partners shall be jointly and severally liable to outsiders for the losses of the partnership business; internally, they shall bear liability in proportion to the debt-sharing ratio or capital contribution ratio agreed upon in the agreement; if the agreement does not specify a debt-sharing ratio or capital contribution ratio, liability shall be borne in proportion to the agreed or actual profit distribution ratio. However, a partner who is at fault for causing losses in the partnership business shall bear correspondingly greater liability according to the degree of fault.

48. A partner who only provides technical services but does not provide funds or tangible property shall also be jointly and severally liable to outsiders for the losses of the partnership business; internally, liability shall be borne in accordance with the debt-sharing ratio agreed upon in the agreement or the capital contribution ratio converted from the technical services; if the agreement does not specify a debt-sharing ratio or capital contribution ratio, liability shall be borne in accordance with the agreed or actual profit distribution ratio among the partners; if there is no profit distribution ratio, liability shall be borne in proportion to the average investment ratio of the other partners.

49. If an individual partnership or an individual industrial and commercial household is erroneously registered by the administrative department for industry and commerce as a collectively owned enterprise, but is in fact an individual partnership or an individual industrial and commercial household, it shall be treated as an individual partnership or an individual industrial and commercial household.

50. If there is no written partnership agreement between the parties, and the parties have not been approved and registered by the administrative department for industry and commerce, but the other conditions for partnership are met, and two or more disinterested persons can prove the existence of an oral partnership agreement, the people's court may find that a partnership relationship exists.

51. Where a partner is added during the process of partnership operation, if the written agreement has provisions, it shall be handled accordingly; if the written agreement does not have provisions, the consent of all partners is required; if consent of all partners is not obtained, the admission of the new partner shall be deemed invalid.

52. Where a partner withdraws from the partnership, if the written agreement has provisions, it shall be handled accordingly; if the written agreement does not have provisions, withdrawal shall generally be permitted. However, if the withdrawal causes losses to other partners, the withdrawing partner's liability for compensation shall be determined by considering the reasons and grounds for withdrawal and the fault of both parties.

53. If losses occur during the partnership operation, and a partner who withdraws from the partnership fails to share the partnership debts as agreed or does not reasonably share them, the withdrawing partner shall remain liable for the discharge of the debts of the original partnership; if the withdrawing partner has already shared the partnership debts, he or she shall still be jointly and severally liable for all debts incurred during his or her participation in the partnership.

54. The partnership property divided upon a partner's withdrawal shall include the property invested at the time of joining the partnership, the property accumulated during the partnership, and the claims and debts during the partnership. The original property contributed upon joining the partnership shall, in principle, be returned upon withdrawal; if a single return is difficult, it may be returned in installments; if returning the original property is indeed difficult, it may be handled by valuation.

55. Upon termination of the partnership, the handling of partnership property shall be in accordance with the written agreement if there is one; if there is no written agreement and consultation fails, if the partners' capital contributions are equal, the matter shall be handled as deemed appropriate by considering the opinions of the majority; if the partners' capital contributions are unequal, the matter may be handled in accordance with the opinion of the partner whose capital contribution accounts for the largest proportion of the total partnership capital, but the interests of the other partners shall be protected.

56. If partners collude with each other to evade partnership debts, in addition to being ordered to bear the liability for discharge, the matter may also be handled in accordance with Paragraph 3 of Article 134 of the General Principles of Civil Law.

57. The phrase "bear liability for discharge with their respective property" in Paragraph 1 of Article 35 of the General Principles of Civil Law means: if a partner contributes with personal property, the partner's personal property shall be used to bear liability; if a partner contributes with the family common property, the family common property shall be used to bear liability; if a partner contributes with personal property, but the profits from the partnership distribution are used for the living expenses of his or her family members, the partner's personal property shall be used first, and the shortfall shall be satisfied with the partner's family common property.

II. Legal Persons

58. Where the legal representative or other staff members of an enterprise legal person engage in business activities in the name of the legal person and cause economic losses to others, the enterprise legal person shall bear civil liability.

59. Where an enterprise legal person is dissolved or is abolished, its competent authority shall organize a liquidation group to carry out liquidation. Where an enterprise legal person is declared bankrupt, the people's court shall organize relevant authorities and relevant persons to establish a liquidation organization to carry out liquidation.

60. A liquidation organization is an organization established according to law for the purpose of liquidating the creditor's rights and debts of an enterprise legal person. It is responsible for the custody, clearance, appraisal, disposal, and satisfaction of the property of a terminated enterprise legal person.

With respect to civil litigation involving the creditor's rights and debts of a terminated enterprise legal person, the liquidation organization may participate in the litigation in its own name.

If a liquidation organization is established for the purpose of evading debt liability, the civil acts it performs shall be void.

61. When trying a case, if the people's court finds that an enterprise legal person has any of the six circumstances listed in Article 49 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, in addition to the enterprise legal person bearing liability, the people's court may also, in accordance with Article 49 and paragraph 3 of Article 134 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, directly impose a fine on the legal representative of the enterprise; if administrative sanctions are required, the court may submit a judicial suggestion to the relevant department for decision and handling; if the act constitutes a crime and criminal liability needs to be pursued according to law, the case shall be transferred to the public security or procuratorial authorities according to law.

62. When imposing sanctions such as fines or detention on a legal representative of an enterprise or other persons according to law in the course of trying a case, the people's court must obtain approval from the president and separately issue a civil sanction decision document. If the person subject to the sanction is dissatisfied with the decision, they may, within ten days from the day following receipt of the decision document, apply to the people's court at the next higher level for reconsideration once. During the reconsideration period, the decision shall not be enforced temporarily.

63. The amount of a fine directly imposed on a legal representative is generally not more than 2,000 yuan, unless otherwise provided by law.

64. A party that contributes the right to use land as a condition for joint operation shall bear the debts of the joint operation enterprise in accordance with the written agreement; if there is no such written agreement, liability may be assumed in proportion to the capital contribution or the profit distribution ratio.

III. Civil Juristic Acts and Agency

65. Where a civil act is performed by means of audio or video recordings or other audiovisual materials, if there are two or more disinterested persons as witnesses or other evidence proving that the civil act complies with the provisions of Article 55 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, it may be recognized as valid.

66. If one party presents a claim for a civil right to the other party, and the other party does not express its opinion clearly in words or in writing, but its conduct indicates acceptance, this may be deemed as tacit acceptance. Tacit inaction may be regarded as an expression of intent only where the law so provides or the parties have so agreed.

67. A civil act performed by an intermittent mental patient, which is proved to have been performed during the period of the illness, shall be recognized as void.

A civil act performed by a person while in a state of unconsciousness shall be recognized as void.

68. Where one party intentionally informs the other party of a false situation, or intentionally conceals the true situation, inducing the other party to make an erroneous expression of intent, it may be recognized as a fraudulent act.

69. Where a party compels the other party to make an expression of intent contrary to its true intention by threatening to cause harm to the life, health, honor, reputation, or property of the citizen or its relatives and friends, or by threatening to cause harm to the honor, reputation, or property of a legal person, it may be recognized as a coercive act.

70. Where one party, taking advantage of the other party's precarious position, seeks improper benefits and compels the other party to make an untrue expression of intent, seriously harming the other party's interests, it may be recognized as taking advantage of another's distress.

71. Where a person makes a mistaken understanding of the nature of the act, the other party, the type, quality, specification, or quantity of the subject matter, and the consequences of the act are contrary to that person's true intention, causing relatively significant loss, it may be recognized as a material misunderstanding.

72. Where one party takes advantage of its superior position or the other party's lack of experience, causing the rights and obligations of the parties to be obviously in violation of the principles of fairness and equivalent compensation, it may be recognized as obvious unfairness.

73. For a civil act involving material misunderstanding or obvious unfairness, if a party requests modification, the people's court shall modify it; if a party requests rescission, the people's court may, at its discretion, modify or rescind it.

Where a party requests modification or rescission of a civil act that is subject to modification or rescission more than one year after the act was established, the people's court shall not protect such request.

74. The phrase "property obtained by both parties" in paragraph 2 of Article 61 of the General Principles of the Civil Law shall include property that has been obtained by both parties and property that they have agreed to obtain.

75. For a conditional civil act, if the condition attached is contrary to legal provisions or is impossible to occur, the civil act shall be recognized as void.

76. A civil juristic act subject to a time condition shall become effective or be terminated upon the arrival of the specified time.

77. Where an expression of intent is gratuitously conveyed by a third party, and the third party mistakenly conveys it due to negligence or fails to convey it, causing loss to others, the person making the expression of intent shall generally be liable for compensation, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties.

78. For a civil act that must be performed personally by the person concerned according to law or the agreement of the parties, if the person concerned does not perform it personally, the act shall be recognized as void.

79. Where several appointed agents exercise the power of agency jointly, and one or several of them, without consulting the other appointed agents, perform an act that infringes upon the rights and interests of the principal, the appointed agent or agents who performed the act shall bear civil liability.

Where there are several principals, and one or several of them, without the consent of the other principals, propose to terminate the agency relationship, thereby causing damage, the principal or principals who proposed the termination shall bear liability.

80. Where, due to special circumstances such as sudden illness or interruption of communication, the appointed agent cannot handle the agency matter itself and cannot promptly contact the principal, and failure to promptly delegate to another agent would cause loss or expand loss to the principal's interests, this constitutes an "emergency situation" as referred to in Article 68 of the General Principles of the Civil Law.

81. Where an appointed agent delegates to another agent, the formalities for delegation shall be handled by analogy with the conditions stipulated in Article 65 of the General Principles of the Civil Law. If loss is caused to a third party due to unclear delegation by the appointed agent, the third party may directly demand compensation from the principal; after the principal assumes civil liability, it may demand compensation from the appointed agent; if the sub-agent is at fault, it shall bear joint and several liability.

82. After the principal's death, the agency acts performed by the appointed agent shall be valid under any of the following circumstances: (1) the agent did not know of the principal's death; (2) all heirs of the principal have ratified the acts; (3) the principal and the agent agreed that the power of agency would terminate upon completion of the agency matter; (4) the acts were commenced before the principal's death and completed after the principal's death for the benefit of the principal's heirs.

83. Where the agent and the principal bear joint and several liability for civil acts already performed, they may be listed as co-litigants in civil proceedings.

IV. Civil Rights

(I) Issues concerning property ownership and property rights related to ownership

84. Where property has been delivered, but the parties have agreed that the transfer of property ownership is subject to a condition, the ownership of the property shall be transferred only when the condition is fulfilled.

85. After the lawful transfer of property ownership, if one party repudiates the transfer, such repudiation shall not be supported. If property ownership has not yet been transferred according to the original agreement, and the party repudiates without legitimate reason, and the agreement can still be performed, it shall continue to be performed; if the agreement cannot be performed, causing loss to the other party, the repudiating party shall be liable for compensation.

86. Where a non-owner adds accessories to another person's property while using it, and the property owner agrees to the addition and has an agreement on how to handle the accessories upon return of the property, the agreement shall be followed; if there is no agreement and negotiation fails, if the accessories can be removed, an order for removal may be made; if they cannot be removed, they may be valued and become the property of the owner; if loss is caused to the property owner, the non-owner shall be liable for compensation.

87. Where property has accessories, the accessories shall be transferred with the transfer of property ownership, unless the parties agree otherwise and such agreement does not violate the law.

88. With respect to common property, if some co-owners claim it is owned in shares and others claim it is jointly owned, if it cannot be proved that the property is owned in shares, it shall be recognized as jointly owned.

89. Joint owners of common property enjoy common rights and bear common obligations. During the existence of the joint ownership relationship, if some co-owners dispose of the common property without authorization, such disposition shall generally be invalid. However, if a third party acquires the property in good faith and for value, the lawful rights and interests of the third party shall be protected; losses of other co-owners shall be compensated by the co-owner who disposed of the property without authorization.

90. Upon the termination of a joint ownership relationship, the division of common property shall be carried out in accordance with the agreement, if any; if there is no agreement, it shall be carried out according to the principle of equal division, taking into account the extent of each co-owner's contribution to the common property and appropriately considering the actual needs of the co-owners for production and living. However, the division of property jointly owned by spouses shall be dealt with in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Marriage Law.

91. Where common property is a specific thing and cannot be divided or division would diminish its value, it may be dealt with by valuation and compensation.

92. After the division of jointly owned common property, if one or several former co-owners sell the property they have received in the division, and the property sold forms an integral part of or is used as a set with the property received by other former co-owners, the claim of those other former co-owners for a preemptive right to purchase shall be supported.

93. Where a citizen or legal person discovers buried or hidden objects that can be proved to belong to it, and such objects may belong to it under current laws and policies, it shall be protected.

94. If found property is lost or damaged, and the finder is not intentional, the finder shall not bear civil liability. If the finder keeps the found property as its own and refuses to return it, resulting in a lawsuit, the case shall be handled as a tort action.

95. The rights and obligations of citizens and collectives to contract for operation of forests, land, hills, grasslands, wasteland, beaches, water surfaces, etc., which are collectively owned or state-owned but used by collectives, shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the contract for operation. Contracts for operation transferred or assigned by the contractor without the consent of the party letting the contract are invalid.

96. Where disputes arise over the ownership or right to use natural resources such as land, hills, forests, grasslands, wasteland, beaches, or water surfaces, the dispute shall be handled by the relevant administrative department. If a party is dissatisfied with the administrative decision, it may file a lawsuit with the people's court in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations; if a lawsuit is filed due to a tort dispute, the people's court may accept it directly.

97. Where an adjacent party temporarily occupies land used by another party for construction, and the occupying party fails to use the land within the scope, purpose, and time limit agreed upon by the parties, it shall be ordered to promptly clean up the site, remove the obstruction, restore the original condition, and compensate for losses.

98. Where one party unilaterally blocks or monopolizes natural flowing water, affecting the normal production or life of another party, the affected party has the right to request removal of the obstruction; if loss is caused, the party causing the blockage shall be liable for compensation.

99. Where an adjacent party must use another party's land to drain water, such use shall be permitted; however, the use shall be within the necessary limits and appropriate protective measures shall be taken for drainage. If loss still results, the beneficiary shall make reasonable compensation.

If an adjacent party could have taken other reasonable measures for drainage but fails to do so, and drains water onto the other party's land, causing or likely causing damage to the other party's property, and the other party requests the injuring party to cease the infringement, eliminate the danger, restore the original condition, or compensate for losses, such request shall be supported.

100. Where one party must pass through land used by an adjacent party, such passage shall be permitted; if loss is thereby caused, appropriate compensation shall be made.

101. With respect to a historically formed necessary passageway within the scope of a building owned or used by a party, the owner or user shall not block it. If blockage affects the production or life of others, and others request removal of the obstruction or restoration of the original condition, such request shall be supported. However, if conditions allow for opening another passageway, such alternative may also be permitted.

102. When handling disputes over dripping water from adjacent houses, the party at fault that caused damage to the other party shall be ordered to remove the obstruction and compensate for losses.

103. Where an adjacent party, on the land it uses, digs drainage ditches, ponds, or cellars, or allows the roots or branches of planted bamboo or trees to extend, endangering the safety or normal use of another party's building, the court shall, depending on the circumstances, order the elimination of the danger, restoration of the original condition, and compensation for losses.

(II) Issues concerning creditor's rights

104. If the creditor refuses without legitimate reason to accept the performance of obligations by the debtor, and the debtor deposits the subject matter of performance with the relevant authority, the debt shall be recognized as performed. The expenses incurred from the deposit shall be borne by the creditor. During the deposit period, the proceeds from the property belong to the creditor, and the risk of loss is borne by the creditor.

105. Pursuant to Article 88, paragraph 2, item (1) of the General Principles of the Civil Law, if the contract does not clearly specify the quality requirements for the product, the parties fail to reach an agreement, and there is no national quality standard, the matter shall be handled according to ministerial standards or professional standards; if there are no ministerial or professional standards, it shall be handled according to approved enterprise standards; if there are no approved enterprise standards, it shall be handled according to the quality standards for similar products approved by other enterprises in the same industry in the place of origin of the subject matter.

106. A surety shall be a citizen, enterprise legal person, or other economic organization with the capacity to compensate. Even if a surety does not have full capacity to compensate, it shall still bear suretyship liability with its own property.

State organs shall not act as sureties.

107. If a branch of an enterprise legal person that does not have the status of a legal person enters into a suretyship contract in its own name, the contract shall generally be recognized as void. However, if the branch has the capacity to pay for the property liability arising therefrom, it shall bear such liability itself; if it has no capacity to pay, the enterprise legal person shall bear the liability.

108. If the surety guarantees to the creditor that the debtor will perform the debt, a written suretyship contract shall be concluded with the creditor, specifying the scope and period of the surety's liability for the principal debt. Even if a separate written suretyship contract is not concluded, if the scope and period of the surety's suretyship are specified in the principal contract and the surety signs or seals it, it shall be deemed that a written suretyship contract has been established. Oral suretyship agreements between citizens, proved by two or more disinterested persons, shall also be deemed as the establishment of a suretyship contract, unless otherwise provided by law.

If the scope of suretyship is unclear, the surety shall be presumed to bear suretyship liability for the entire principal debt.

109. Within the suretyship period, the scope of the surety's liability may be reduced as the principal debt decreases. For newly added debts, unless the surety has agreed to provide guarantee, the surety shall not bear suretyship liability.

110. If there are two or more sureties, they shall bear joint and several suretyship liability, unless the sureties have agreed with the creditor to assume liability in shares.

111. After the economic contract guaranteed is confirmed to be void, if the guaranteed party needs to return property or compensate for losses, the surety shall still bear joint and several liability unless otherwise specially agreed.

112. When the debtor or a third party provides collateral to the creditor, a written contract shall be concluded or the matter shall be stated in the original debt document. If there is no written contract, but other evidence proves that the collateral or the certificate of title thereto has been delivered to the mortgagee, the mortgage relationship may be recognized as established.

113. If property over which one does not enjoy ownership or the right to manage is used as collateral, the mortgage shall be recognized as void.

If property whose circulation is restricted by law is used as collateral, the relevant authority shall purchase it at the time of debt satisfaction, and the mortgagee may be repaid in priority from the proceeds.

114. If the collateral is lost or damaged during the period when it is in the custody of the mortgagee, and the mortgagee is at fault, the mortgagee shall bear civil liability.

If the collateral is lost or damaged while in the possession of the mortgagor, the mortgage relationship shall be deemed to exist, and the mortgagor shall be ordered to replace the collateral with other property.

115. If the collateral is possessed and kept by the mortgagor, and during the mortgage term, without the creditor's consent, the mortgagor transfers the same collateral to another person, or re-mortgages the portion of the collateral's value already subject to the mortgage, such act shall be void.

When the debtor uses the collateral to satisfy the debt, if there are several mortgagees for the same collateral, they shall be repaid in the order in which the mortgages were established.

116. Where there are several creditors, including creditors claiming repayment of bank loans and other debts, the creditor with a mortgage right shall be entitled to priority in repayment, unless otherwise provided by laws or regulations.

117. If the creditor holds property of the debtor due to a contractual relationship, and the debtor fails to perform its obligations at maturity, the creditor may retain the corresponding property. After a demand, if the debtor still fails to perform its obligations within a reasonable period, and the creditor sells the retained property at a reasonable price according to law and is repaid in priority from the sale proceeds, such act shall be protected.

118. If the lessor sells a leased house, it shall notify the lessee three months in advance. The lessee has a preemptive right to purchase under the same conditions; if the lessor sells the house without complying with this provision, the lessee may request the people's court to declare the sale of the house void.

119. If a lessee rents a private house in its own name, and the lessee dies during the lease term, the persons living together with the lessee in the same household may demand to continue performing the original lease, and such demand shall be permitted.

If the ownership of a private house is transferred during the lease term due to sale, gift, or inheritance, the original lease contract shall continue to be valid between the lessee and the new owner.

If no lease term is fixed, and the house owner demands to take back the house for self-occupation, such demand shall generally be permitted. If the lessee is able to move, the lessee shall be ordered to move; if the lessee has genuine difficulty in moving, a certain period may be granted for the lessee to find another house or to vacate part of the house.

120. During the period of house chattel mortgage or upon expiration of the mortgage term, if the parties agree to extend the mortgage term or increase or decrease the mortgage price, such agreement shall be permitted. If the mortgagee demands that the mortgagor redeem the property at a price higher than the original mortgage price, such demand shall generally not be supported. If lawful circulating goods are used as the mortgage price, the redemption price shall be calculated based on the retail market price at the time of redemption.

121. With respect to loans between citizens, if the parties have agreed on the term for repayment, it shall generally be handled according to the agreement; if there is no agreement, the lender may demand repayment at any time, and the borrower shall repay promptly upon the lender's demand; if the borrower is temporarily unable to repay, the borrower may be ordered to repay in installments according to the actual circumstances.

122. The interest rate for production or business loans between citizens may be appropriately higher than that for living loans. If a dispute arises over the interest rate, it shall be handled in accordance with the principles of protecting lawful loan relationships, considering the actual local circumstances, and benefiting production and stabilizing the economic order.

123. For an interest-free loan between citizens, if a repayment term has been agreed and the borrower fails to repay on time, or if no repayment term has been agreed but the borrower still fails to repay after being demanded by the lender, and the lender requests the borrower to pay overdue interest, such request shall be permitted.

124. If the parties to a loan dispute over the interest rate and the agreement is unclear and cannot be proved, the interest may be calculated by reference to the interest rate on similar loans from banks.

125. With respect to loans between citizens, if the lender includes the interest in the principal to calculate compound interest, such practice shall not be protected; if the interest is deducted at the time of lending, the interest shall be calculated based on the actual amount lent.

126. Where a tangible item is borrowed, the lender's request for return of the original item or an item of the same quantity and quality shall be supported; if it is truly impossible to return the original item, compensation may be made at the market retail price at the time of return or at a price slightly higher than that.

127. If the borrowed item is damaged due to the borrower's improper management or use, the borrower shall bear liability for compensation; if the borrowed item itself has defects, the borrower's liability for compensation may be reduced.

128. The formation of a gift relationship between citizens is based on delivery of the gift. For a gift of a house, if the transfer of ownership has been completed pursuant to a written gift contract, the gift relationship shall be deemed established; if the transfer of ownership has not been completed, but the donor has delivered the title deed to the donee pursuant to a written gift contract, and the donee has taken possession and used the house pursuant to the gift contract, the gift may be deemed valid, but the donee shall be ordered to complete the transfer of ownership procedures.

129. If the donor clearly indicates that the gift is given to a minor personally, the gift shall be deemed the minor's personal property.

130. If a donor transfers property to another person in order to evade a legal obligation that should be performed, and an interested person asserts rights, the gift shall be deemed invalid.

131. Unjust enrichment to be returned shall include the original property and any fruits derived therefrom. Other benefits obtained by taking advantage of the unjust enrichment, after deducting management expenses and labor costs, shall be confiscated.

132. The manager or service provider referred to in Article 93 of the General Principles of the Civil Law may claim from the beneficiary the necessary expenses, including direct expenses incurred in the management or service activities, as well as actual losses suffered in such activities.

(III) Issues Concerning Intellectual Property and Personal Rights

133. Whether a work is published or not, the author enjoys copyright.

134. If two or more persons jointly create a work in accordance with an agreement, regardless of the extent to which each person's creative results are adopted in the work, the work shall be deemed a joint creation.

135. For a jointly authored work, the copyright shall be deemed jointly owned by all co-authors; if the component parts can exist independently, the copyright in each component part shall be owned separately by the author of that part.

136. After the author's death, if the property rights in the copyright that are inheritable are infringed within the statutory protection period, and the heir requests protection in accordance with the law, the People's Court shall support such request.

137. Patent rights obtained by citizens or legal persons through patent application, or through inheritance, gift, assignment, or other means, shall be protected.
The assignment of a patent right shall be registered and announced by the Patent Office of the State; the patent right shall be transferred from the date of announcement by the Patent Office of the State.

138. The exclusive right to use a trademark obtained by a legal person, individual business, or partnership through trademark registration application or assignment, unless revoked in accordance with legal procedures, shall be protected.
The assignment of the exclusive right to use a trademark shall be approved by the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce; the exclusive right to use a trademark shall be transferred from the date of approval.

139. Using a citizen's portrait for advertisements, trademarks, window displays, etc., without the citizen's consent for profit-making purposes, shall be deemed an infringement of the citizen's right to portrait.

140. Publicizing another person's privacy in written or oral form, fabricating facts to openly defame another person's personality, or damaging another person's reputation through insults, slander, or other means, causing certain influence, shall be deemed an infringement of the citizen's right to reputation.
Using written or oral form to slander or defame the reputation of a legal person, causing damage to the legal person, shall be deemed an infringement of the legal person's right to reputation.

141. Using another person's name or title without authorization or counterfeiting it, causing damage, shall be deemed an infringement of the right to name or title.

V. Civil Liability

142. Where a person suffers damage while safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of the state, the collective, or another person, if the tortfeasor is unable to compensate or there is no tortfeasor, the People's Court may, upon the victim's request, order the beneficiary to provide appropriate compensation based on the benefit received by the beneficiary and the beneficiary's financial condition.

143. The period of absence from work due to injury shall be determined based on the actual degree of harm, the recovery condition, and the certificate from the treating hospital or forensic authentication. The standard for compensation may be calculated according to the victim's wage standard or actual income.
If the victim is a contracted household or an individual business, the calculation standard for compensation for absence from work may be determined with reference to the victim's average income over a certain period. If the victim's contracted planting or aquaculture industry is highly seasonal, and delay in operation would cause greater losses, in addition to the victim taking measures to prevent loss expansion, the People's Court may also order the tortfeasor to take measures to prevent loss expansion.

144. Compensation for medical treatment expenses shall generally be based on the diagnosis certificate from the local treating hospital and the receipts for medical expenses and hospitalization expenses. Expenses for treatment at another hospital without approval from the medical department shall generally not be compensated; expenses for self-purchased medicines unrelated to the injury or for treating other diseases shall not be compensated.

145. For a person specially authorized by the hospital to provide nursing care, compensation for loss of work may be calculated based on the actual loss of income. Bonuses that should have been received may generally be included in the amount of compensation. If the person has no salary income, the compensation standard shall be limited to the wage standard for general temporary workers in the locality.

146. Where a person's body is injured causing total or partial loss of labor capacity, the living subsidy compensation shall generally be sufficient to reach no less than the standard of basic living expenses for local residents.

147. Where a person's body is injured causing death or loss of labor capacity, and a person who was actually supported by the victim and has no other source of livelihood requests necessary living expenses from the tortfeasor, such request shall be supported, and the amount shall be determined according to actual circumstances.

148. A person who instigates or assists another person to commit a tortious act shall be a joint tortfeasor and bear joint and several civil liability.
A person who instigates or assists a person with no civil capacity to commit a tortious act shall be a tortfeasor and bear civil liability.
A person who instigates or assists a person with limited civil capacity to commit a tortious act shall be a joint tortfeasor and bear primary civil liability.

149. Using another person's name without authorization or counterfeiting it, to deceive or mock others by letters, telegrams, or other means, causing damage to their property or reputation, the tortfeasor shall bear civil liability.

150. Where a citizen's right to name, portrait, reputation, or honor, or a legal person's right to name, reputation, or honor is infringed, and the citizen or legal person requests compensation for losses, the People's Court may determine the amount of compensation based on the degree of fault of the tortfeasor, the specific circumstances of the tortious act, and the consequences and impact.

151. Where a person profits by infringing another person's right to name, title, portrait, reputation, or honor, in addition to compensating the victim for losses in accordance with the law, the illegal gains shall be confiscated.

152. Where a state organ's staff member causes damage to the legitimate rights and interests of a citizen or legal person in the performance of official duties, the state organ shall bear civil liability.

153. Where a consumer or user suffers personal injury or property loss to themselves or a third party due to the use of a product of substandard quality, the victim may claim compensation from the manufacturer or seller. A lawsuit filed on this basis shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the location of the defendant or the place where the tortious act occurred.
If the carrier or warehouser bears responsibility for the product quality, and the manufacturer or seller claims compensation for losses, it may be handled in a separate case, or the carrier and warehouser may be listed as third parties and handled together.

154. Where a person engaged in high-risk activities fails to take necessary safety and protective measures as required by relevant regulations, seriously threatening the personal or property safety of others, the People's Court shall, upon the request of the other person, order the operator to eliminate the danger.

155. Where damage is caused to another person by the collapse of piled items, if none of the parties is at fault, it shall be handled appropriately based on the principle of fairness.

156. Where damage is caused to another person by an act of necessity to avert an imminent danger, if the danger arose from natural causes and the actor's measures were not improper, the actor shall not bear civil liability. If the victim requests compensation, the beneficiary may be ordered to provide appropriate compensation.

157. Where none of the parties is at fault for the damage, but one party suffers damage in the course of activities for the benefit of the other party or for common interests, the other party or the beneficiary may be ordered to provide certain economic compensation.

158. After a husband and wife divorce, if a minor child infringes upon the rights and interests of another person, the parent living with the child shall bear civil liability; if it is truly difficult for that parent to bear civil liability alone, the parent not living with the child may be ordered to bear civil liability jointly.

159. Where a person under guardianship causes damage to another person, if there is a clear guardian, the guardian shall bear civil liability; if the guardian is unclear, the person with guardianship ability in the order of priority shall bear civil liability.

160. If a person with no civil capacity who lives and studies in a kindergarten or school, or a mental patient receiving treatment in a psychiatric hospital, suffers injury or causes damage to another person, and the unit is at fault, the unit may be ordered to provide appropriate compensation.

161. If at the time of the tortious act the actor was under 18 years old, but at the time of the lawsuit has reached 18 years old and has economic capacity, the actor shall bear civil liability; if the actor has no economic capacity, the former guardian shall bear civil liability.
If the actor was 18 years old or older at the time of causing damage, the actor shall bear civil liability personally; if the actor has no income, the supporter shall advance the payment; if advance payment is difficult, deferred payment may be ordered or mediated.

162. During litigation, if there is a situation requiring cessation of infringement, removal of obstacles, or elimination of danger, the People's Court may, upon application by the party or ex officio, issue a preliminary ruling.
If a party has assumed civil liability by way of apology during the litigation, it shall be stated in the judgment.

163. During litigation, if illegal activities related to the case are discovered that require sanctions, Article 134, Paragraph 3 of the General Principles of the Civil Law may be applied to impose admonition, order a statement of repentance, confiscate property and illegal gains used in illegal activities, or impose a fine or detention in accordance with the law.
Sanctions of confiscation, fine, or detention must be approved by the president of the court, and a separate civil sanction decision shall be made. If the sanctioned person contests the decision, they may apply for reconsideration to the next higher People's Court within ten days from the day following receipt of the decision. During the reconsideration period, the decision shall not be executed temporarily.

164. The amount of a fine imposed on a citizen under Article 134, Paragraph 3 of the General Principles of the Civil Law shall not exceed RMB 500, and detention shall not exceed 15 days.
Detention sanctions imposed on a legal representative in accordance with the law shall not exceed 15 days.
The above two paragraphs do not apply where the law provides otherwise.

VI. Statute of Limitations

165. For rights that the obligee knew or should have known were infringed before the implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the statute of limitations for seeking protection from the People's Court after implementation shall be governed by Articles 135 and 136 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, calculated from January 1, 1987.

166. For civil rights infringed more than 20 years before the implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the statute of limitations for the obligee to seek protection from the People's Court after implementation shall be, respectively, the two-year period under Article 135 or the one-year period under Article 136 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, calculated from January 1, 1987.

167. After the implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law, if the statute of limitations is the two-year period under Article 135, and the obligee only becomes aware of the infringement between the 18th and 20th year after the infringement, or if the statute of limitations is the one-year period under Article 136, and the obligee only becomes aware of the infringement between the 19th and 20th year after the infringement, the right to file a lawsuit shall be exercised within 20 years from the date of infringement; if more than 20 years have passed, protection shall not be granted.

168. For the statute of limitations for personal injury compensation, if the injury is obvious, it shall be calculated from the date of injury; if the injury was not discovered at the time but later diagnosed and proven to be caused by the infringement, it shall be calculated from the date of diagnosis.

169. Where the obligee cannot exercise the right of claim within the statutory statute of limitations due to objective obstacles, this constitutes a "special circumstance" under Article 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law.

170. If state property not authorized for management or operation by citizens or legal persons is infringed, the statute of limitations does not apply.

171. After the statute of limitations has expired, if the obligor performs the obligation and later reneges on the grounds that the statute of limitations has expired, such reneging shall not be supported.

172. Within the last six months of the statute of limitations, if a person with no civil capacity or limited civil capacity whose rights were infringed has no legal representative, or the legal representative has died or lost the power of representation, or the legal representative personally has lost capacity, it may be deemed that the right of claim cannot be exercised due to other obstacles, and the suspension of statute of limitations applies.

173. After the statute of limitations is interrupted by the obligee asserting rights or the obligor agreeing to perform the obligation, if the obligee again asserts rights or the obligor again agrees to perform the obligation within the new statute of limitations period, it may be deemed that the statute of limitations is interrupted again.
If the obligee asserts rights against the debtor's guarantor, the debtor's agent, or the property custodian, the statute of limitations may be deemed interrupted.

174. If the obligee submits a request for protection of civil rights to the People's Mediation Committee or a relevant unit, the statute of limitations is interrupted from the time of the request. If mediation fails to reach an agreement, the statute of limitations period shall be recalculated from that time; if an agreement is reached through mediation but the obligor fails to perform within the period specified in the agreement, the statute of limitations period shall be recalculated from the expiration of that period.

175. The statute of limitations periods provided in Articles 135 and 136 of the General Principles of the Civil Law may be subject to the provisions on suspension, interruption, and extension under the General Principles of the Civil Law.
The "20-year" statute of limitations period provided in Article 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law may be subject to the provisions on extension under the General Principles of the Civil Law, but not to the provisions on suspension and interruption.

176. Where laws or regulations have special provisions on the time for claiming compensation or for raising objections to product quality, such special provisions shall apply.

177. The statute of limitations for inheritance shall be governed by the Inheritance Law. However, after the inheritance commences, if the heir does not explicitly renounce the inheritance, it shall be deemed acceptance of the inheritance; if the estate has not been divided, it shall be deemed co-ownership. The suspension, interruption, and extension of the statute of limitations shall apply the relevant provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law.

VII. Application of Law to Foreign-Related Civil Relations

178. A civil relation is foreign-related if one or both parties are foreigners, stateless persons, or foreign legal persons; if the subject matter of the civil relation is located in a foreign territory; or if the legal facts that give rise to, change, or extinguish the civil rights and obligations occur in a foreign country.
When a People's Court hears a case involving foreign-related civil relations, it shall determine the applicable substantive law in accordance with Chapter VIII of the General Principles of the Civil Law.

179. For the capacity for civil conduct of a Chinese citizen residing abroad, if the act is performed within Chinese territory, Chinese law shall apply; if performed in the country of residence, the law of that country may apply.

180. When a foreigner engages in civil activities within Chinese territory, if the foreigner has no capacity for civil conduct under the law of his or her home country but has capacity under Chinese law, the foreigner shall be deemed to have capacity for civil conduct.

181. For the capacity for civil conduct of a stateless person, the law of the country of residence shall generally apply; if not resident, the law of the country of domicile shall apply.

182. For a foreigner with dual or multiple nationalities, the law of the country where the foreigner has a domicile or the country with which the foreigner has the closest connection shall be deemed the law of the home country.

183. If a party's domicile is unknown or cannot be determined, the place of habitual residence shall be deemed the domicile. If a party has multiple domiciles, the domicile with the closest connection to the civil relation giving rise to the dispute shall be the domicile.

184. The law of the country where a foreign legal person is registered shall be deemed the law of the home country of that legal person, and the capacity for civil conduct of the legal person shall be determined according to that law.
Civil activities carried out by a foreign legal person within Chinese territory must comply with Chinese laws and regulations.

185. If a party has two or more business establishments, the establishment with the closest connection to the civil relation giving rise to the dispute shall be the determining factor; if the party has no business establishment, the domicile or habitual residence shall be the determining factor.

186. Land, buildings attached to land, other fixtures, and fixed accessory equipment of buildings are immovable property. Civil relations concerning ownership, sale, lease, mortgage, use, etc., of immovable property shall be governed by the law of the place where the immovable property is located.

187. The law of the place of the tortious act includes the law of the place where the tortious act was committed and the law of the place where the consequences of the tort occurred. If the two differ, the People's Court may choose to apply one of them.

188. For foreign-related divorce cases accepted by Chinese courts, the divorce and the division of property arising from the divorce shall be governed by Chinese law. The validity of the marriage shall be governed by the law of the place where the marriage was concluded.

189. Maintenance between parents and children, between spouses, and between other persons with a maintenance relationship shall be governed by the law of the country with which the person to be maintained has the closest connection. The nationality and domicile of the maintenance obligor and the person to be maintained, and the location of the property supporting the person to be maintained, may all be deemed as having the closest connection with the person to be maintained.

190. The establishment, modification, and termination of guardianship shall be governed by the law of the home country of the ward. However, if the ward has a domicile within Chinese territory, Chinese law shall apply.

191. For the property left by a foreigner who died within Chinese territory, if there is no heir and no legatee, it shall be handled in accordance with Chinese law, unless otherwise provided by international treaties concluded or acceded to by the two countries.

192. Where foreign law should be applied according to law, and different regions of that foreign country have different laws, the applicable law shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of that country on the adjustment of domestic legal conflicts. If such provisions do not exist, the law of the region with the closest connection to the civil relation shall be directly applied.

193. Foreign law that should be applied may be ascertained through the following channels: (1) provided by the parties; (2) provided by the central authority of the contracting party that has concluded a judicial assistance agreement with China; (3) provided by the Chinese embassy or consulate in that country; (4) provided by the embassy of that country in China; (5) provided by Chinese and foreign legal experts. If the foreign law cannot be ascertained through the above channels, the law of the People's Republic of China shall apply.

194. If a party evades the application of mandatory or prohibitive legal norms of China, the act shall not have the effect of applying foreign law.

195. The statute of limitations for foreign-related civil legal relations shall be determined by the lex causae of the civil legal relationship as determined by the conflict rules.

VIII. Other Provisions

196. For cases accepted after January 1, 1987, if the civil act occurred before 1987, the laws and policies in effect at the time of the civil act shall apply; if no specific provisions existed in the laws and policies at that time, the General Principles of Civil Law may be applied by analogy.

197. In handling petition cases and cases retried under the trial supervision procedure, the laws or policies that should have been applied at the time of conclusion of the original trial shall apply.

198. Where the period agreed upon by the parties does not commence from the first day of a month or year, a month shall be thirty days, and a year shall be three hundred and sixty-five days.

If the last day of a period falls on a Sunday or other statutory holiday, and the Sunday or other statutory holiday has been adjusted, the day following the actual day of rest shall be deemed the last day of the period.

199. Where the parties have agreed on the method of calculation for a period calculated in days, months, or years, such agreement shall prevail.

200. Where previous relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court conflict with the General Principles of Civil Law and these Opinions, the people's courts at all levels shall no longer apply such previous provisions when hearing civil cases and economic dispute cases of first and second instance from now on.
